title: Week Ahead: US CPI, Big Bank Earnings and TSMC in Focus
summary: September CPI, earnings from JPMorgan to TSMC, and Fed signals drive US stocks this week. Here is the calendar and the stocks to watch.
body_markdown:
Fed officials are also scheduled to speak almost every day, including the Fed Chair on Friday. Their tone after the CPI release could shift rate expectations quickly.


Wednesday's Beige Book offers a snapshot of conditions across the Fed's 12 districts. It may show how policymakers read the impact of high energy prices on businesses and consumers.


Thursday's data also matters. Core PPI is forecast to rise 0.3% MoM from 0.2%, a signal of whether price pressure at the producer level is still building.


Retail Sales are expected to slow to 0.3% after last month's 1.2% jump. A sharper slowdown could suggest US consumers are starting to pull back as energy costs stay high.


## Stocks to Watch


Q3 2026 earnings season officially starts this week, and expectations are already high. The spotlight is on banks and semiconductors.


**Wall Street's big banks**


Four major banks report before the open on Tuesday, with these consensus EPS estimates:


- [JPMorgan Chase (JPM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/jpm/) : around $5.93 per share.
- [Goldman Sachs (GS)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/gs/) : around $13.04 per share.
- [Citigroup (C)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/c/) : around $2.65 per share.
- [Wells Fargo (WFC)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/wfc/) : around $1.85 per share.


Reports continue on Wednesday and Thursday:


- [Bank of America (BAC)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/bac/) (Wednesday): EPS estimate around $1.10.
- [Morgan Stanley (MS)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/ms/) (Wednesday): EPS estimate around $2.93.
- [BlackRock (BLK)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/blk/) (Wednesday): EPS estimate around $14.30.
- [Charles Schwab (SCHW)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/schw/) (Thursday): EPS estimate around $1.66.


The numbers to watch are net interest income and credit quality. Higher rates can widen lending margins, but they also raise the risk of bad loans.


For JPMorgan, analysts expect net interest income to grow about 12%, while trading revenue is expected to decline. Management's view on the US economy will be closely watched.


Bank results often act as a mirror of the broader economy. If lenders see consumers and businesses holding up well, that could support wider market sentiment.


**Healthcare**


[UnitedHealth (UNH)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/unh/) and[Johnson & Johnson (JNJ)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/jnj/) are also scheduled to report on Tuesday. Both offer a read on defensive sectors at a time when investors are wary of high rates.


**TSMC**


[Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tsm/) reports before the US open on Thursday, with an EPS estimate of around $4.48 per ADR. For AI-linked stocks, this may be the most important report of the week.


Investors will focus on TSMC's AI revenue outlook and capital spending plans. Solid numbers could ease worries about AI chip demand, while weak guidance could weigh on the semiconductor sector.


## Market Sentiment


US stocks enter this week in an unusual position. Major indexes sit near records despite three heavy pressures at once:


- **High oil prices:** Brent is holding around $100 a barrel amid an energy shock tied to the conflict involving Iran.
- **High bond yields:** The 10-year Treasury yield is holding above 5%, near its highest level in more than two decades.
- **A hawkish Fed:** Most Fed officials expect further rate hikes before year-end.


AI sentiment also wobbled last week. On Thursday, the Nasdaq fell more than 1% on concerns that OpenAI's revenue was falling short of targets.


Stocks recovered on Friday, with the S&P 500 up 0.4% and the Nasdaq up 0.6%. The rebound followed reports that OpenAI expects annualized revenue to reach or exceed $70 billion by year-end.


Even so, the market remains highly sensitive to AI headlines. We see this week's sentiment as neutral, with a cautious tilt.


Three simple scenarios can help frame the week:


- **Hot CPI and weak bank guidance:** profit-taking could pick up, especially in richly valued tech stocks.
- **In-line CPI:** attention shifts to earnings details, so moves may vary more from stock to stock.
- **Softer CPI and strong TSMC results:** the rally toward new records could extend.


Expect higher volatility, particularly around Wednesday's CPI release.
